thread:
michael: heads up — noticed a 20-30% throughput drop on the 8xA100 cluster when we enable LLProto + channel=8 for tensor-parallel workloads. this started after yesterday's kernel selector tweak.
anya: hmm, saw something similar on staging this morning. end-to-end p99 ok but overall tokens/sec down. any traces?
michael: grabbed an nvprof/NSYS snapshot. key bits:
```
# nsys summary
allreduce_avg_latency_ms: 1.32
allreduce_tail_95_ms: 4.8
nccl_channels: 8
proto: enabled
ll128: disabled
kernel_selector: dynamic_v2
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.82
batching_mean_seq: 64
```
There's a lot more CUDA stall time during KV cache warmup and frequent small allreduces.
raph: that avg allreduce latency seems high for intra-node 8x A100. are those small-message allreduces triggering proto fallback?
michael: looks like proto is choosing algo=ring for some sizes, and LL128 isn't being used. profiler shows a bunch of tiny messages (~512B-2KB) hitting the allreduce hot path.
sanjay: could be channel starvation. with channel=8 and dynamic_v2 kernel selector we might be splitting work across channels unevenly — smaller fragments end up serialized.
anya: can you paste the trace of per-channel bandwidth from NSYS? also include per-CPU thread assignment.
michael: paste from trace analyzer (simplified):
```
channel 0 bw: 180GB/s active 72%
channel 1 bw: 10GB/s active 5%
channel 2 bw: 160GB/s active 65%
channel 3 bw: 8GB/s active 4%
channel 4 bw: 170GB/s active 68%
channel 5 bw: 12GB/s active 6%
channel 6 bw: 165GB/s active 66%
channel 7 bw: 9GB/s active 4%
```
So it's extremely imbalanced.
raph: yep that's classic mapping skew. Looks like proto mapping strategy is producing long stride between fragments. could be stride=128 -> poor packing.
anya: what about kernel selection logs? does dynamic_v2 prefer certain kernels for small seq lengths?
michael: dynamic_v2 picks kernel K3 for seq<=32, K5 for 33-128, K7 for >128. but K3 forces LLProto to fragment into many tiny collectives.
sanjay: two quick experiments to try: 1) reduce nccl channels to 4 and compare 2) force LL128 for small messages (bypass proto) and measure. both cheap.
perf-bot: nightly-regression: 2026-03-17 03:12 UTC — perf-suite/llproto-wavefront: throughput -22% (p50 tokens/sec). full artifacts: s3://perf-artifacts/2026-03-17/2187654321/
anya: thanks perf-bot. michael — can you run with envs: NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=0 NCCL_PROTO=LL128 NCCL_CHANNELS=4 and kernel_selector=dynamic_v2 but with a patched fragmenter that prefers contiguous chunks?
michael: running now on canary. quick numbers:
- baseline (ch=8, proto=auto): 920 tokens/sec
- ch=4, proto=LL128: 1180 tokens/sec
- ch=8, proto=LL128: 1150 tokens/sec
- ch=8, proto=auto + fragmenter-stride=32: 1120 tokens/sec
so forcing LL128 or reducing channels both recover most of the loss.
raph: interesting that ch=8+LL128 is slightly worse than ch=4+LL128. implies channel overhead/lock contention even when proto good.
anya: agree. for smaller messages, more channels hurts due to extra NCCL context switches. we should extend kernel selector cost model to include model of per-channel overhead vs message size.
sanjay: also KV cache behavior — kv_cache_hit_rate was 0.82. when cache warms, we see more small messages; maybe batching heuristic needs to wait for stable prefix before aggressive batching.
michael: good call. I also profiled kernel selection decisions during warmup: the selector switches kernels mid-request because effective sequence length varies a lot between tokens. that triggers kernel rebinds and KV eviction churn.
anya: proposed action items:
- short: set default NCCL_CHANNELS=4 for prod TP configs when avg message < 256KB (flags + override in runtime).
- medium: update kernel_selector to penalize channel-heavy configs for small-message distributions and add a fragmentation heuristic (max_frag_size=32KB).
- long: add a microbench harness to simulate KV cache warmup patterns and autotune proto/algo per workload.
raph: i'll open a perf task and assign. also let's add a tracing hook to collect per-fragment mapping to channels so we can correlate fragment size -> channel imbalance.
sanjay: i'll run a sweep across our fleet for the last 48h to see where this config would have improved throughput.
michael: ok i'll push a canary patch to runtime that sets NCCL_CHANNELS env based on observed median fragment size and rolls to canary. will attach traces.
anya: awesome. @perf-bot can you schedule a focused integration test that runs small-message TP runs with both proto=auto and proto=LL128 and reports p50/p90 tokens/sec?
perf-bot: scheduled: perf-suite/llproto-wavefront-retest on 2026-03-18 04:00 UTC. results will be posted in this thread. :gear: :bar_chart:
raph: thanks everyone. this felt like the classic interaction of kernel selector + proto + channel count + kv warmup. nice root cause. we'll follow up with PRs for selector cost model and the fragmentation probe.
michael: thanks — attaching canary logs once upload completes.
sanjay: great work. hope the canary looks clean. :thumbsup:
